title: Usability Testing
body:
**Usability testing** puts real users in front of the system with real tasks and observes what
happens. It is the only evaluation method producing evidence about behaviour, where the others
produce expert judgement, which is why it outranks the others despite costing more.

The procedure:

```
1. recruit users who match the User Persona and were not involved in the design
2. give a task, phrased as a goal          "find out how much you owe this month"
3. stay silent and watch
4. record: completed or not, time taken, errors, where they hesitated
5. debrief afterwards, once the observation is finished
```

Step 3 is the discipline the whole method depends on. A facilitator who explains has answered
the question the test was asking, and the recording is then evidence about the explanation. The
instruction to think aloud is the exception, since a running commentary reveals what the user
believed was happening.

The output is quantitative and comparable, which is what allows two designs to be judged on
evidence:

```
task completion rate     the fraction who finished unaided
time on task             median, since one lost user distorts a mean
error count              actions that had to be undone or repeated
```

Five users find most of the problems, which is the counterintuitive result of the field, since
problems are not evenly distributed and the frequent ones appear immediately. Testing twenty
users mostly re-finds what the first five found.

Comparing two designs on task time is a statistical claim, so [[Hypothesis Testing]] in
[[STATISTICS]] is what supports it, and observing users who helped build the thing produces the
[[Cognitive Bias]] that [[INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY AND SOCIETY]] describes.
